title: Longtime sports analyst Rob Parker not sold that Red Sox will make playoffs
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Rob Parker doubts Boston Red Sox will maintain their performance and make the 2026 playoffs.
Boston Red Sox secured the second A.L. wild-card spot, with FanGraphs giving them a 96% playoff chance.
Red Sox achieved record-breaking stats, including winning 32 of their last 38 games since late June.

title: Chad Tracy ‘hopeful’ Wilyer Abreu is back in Red Sox lineup Sunday
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Wilyer Abreu was a late scratch from the Red Sox lineup Saturday due to leg swelling.
Chad Tracy is hopeful Abreu will return for Sunday's game against the Athletics after receiving treatment.
Abreu has hit 20 home runs with 62 RBIs, achieving a .256 average and .793 OPS this season.

title: Red Sox’ latest winning streak ends at 9 games after loss to Athletics
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Red Sox lose 7-3 to Athletics, snapping their nine-game winning streak.
Jake Bennett allowed four earned runs over 5.1 innings in his 13th start of the season.
Red Sox retain the second wild-card spot in the American League, 1.5 games behind the Yankees.

title: Here’s why Gillette Stadium is swapping out its turf surface again so soon after the World Cup
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Gillette Stadium will install new turf before the Patriots' preseason game due to an NFL policy.
The current turf, installed after the World Cup, lacks NFL laboratory testing approval due to procedural timing.
Kraft Sports Group requested an updated test, but the NFL denied it until 2027's procedural window.

title: 4 takeaways from the Revolution’s loss vs. Houston Dynamo
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: New England Revolution lost 2-0 to Houston Dynamo at Gillette Stadium, spoiling Jack Harrison's club debut.
Houston's Guilherme and Agustin Resch scored, capitalizing on New England's defensive lapses and effective counter-attacks.
Despite lively play, Harrison couldn't immediately impact the game; the Revolution's attack struggled to find openings.

title: Here’s the latest injury updates on Roman Anthony, Adley Rutschman
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Roman Anthony has been out since May with a wrist injury, currently hitting off a pitching machine to ramp up.
Adley Rutschman, acquired by the Red Sox, is closer to returning, having started a rehab assignment with Worcester.
The Red Sox, on a 9-game winning streak, anticipate further improvements with Anthony and Rutschman's returns.

title: New on Netflix and more: Top streaming picks for August 2026
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'Clueless', 'Eighth Grade', and 'Something's Gotta Give' are streaming on Netflix this month.
'Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender' movie premieres August 2026 on Paramount+.
'The Ballad of Wallis Island' and 'You, Me & Tuscany' available on Peacock.

title: An 8-foot Bigfoot was spotted in Connecticut last month. It’s far from New England’s first.
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Kevin Klimas reported an eight-foot Bigfoot sighting in Voluntown, Connecticut on July 5, verified by the BFRO.
Since 1994, 126 verified Bigfoot sightings have occurred in New England, according to the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization.
Despite numerous reports, scientists like BU's Eva Garrett remain skeptical due to lack of concrete evidence of Bigfoot's existence.

title: I will miss my friend Margo, who told me to grieve, but not too much
author: Meredith Goldstein
bullets: Margo Howard, daughter of Ann Landers, passed away at 86, known for her empathetic yet direct advice columns.
Margo wrote the Dear Prudence column for Slate and Dear Margo for The Boston Globe, exuding confidence and sarcasm.
The author recalls Margo's advice on embracing joy after loss and cherishing fond memories without excessive grieving.

title: Red Sox bats, Payton Tolle’s 14 strikeouts stifle Athletics, 13-1
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Payton Tolle recorded a career-high 14 strikeouts, leading the Red Sox to a 13-1 win over the Athletics.
Boston extended their winning streak to nine games and totaled 15 hits in the dominant victory.
Newcomer Raymond Burgos pitched three innings without allowing a hit or walk in his debut for the Red Sox.
